Magic Kingdom.text: Florida's high water table kept its staff tunnels above ground, so the park is built on the second story.
Magic Kingdom.evidence: Because of Florida's high water table, the tunnels could not be put underground, so they were built at the existing grade, meaning the park is built on the second story, giving Magic Kingdom an elevation of 108 feet (33 m).

Disneyland.text: Walt Disney got the idea while watching his daughters ride the merry-go-round at Griffith Park.
Disneyland.evidence: The concept for Disneyland began when Walt Disney was visiting Griffith Park in Los Angeles with his daughters Diane and Sharon. While watching them ride the merry-go-round, he came up with the idea of a place where adults and their children could go and have fun together, though this idea lay dormant for many years.

Universal Studios Japan.text: Ahead of its opening, All Nippon Airways unveiled a Woody Woodpecker-themed "Woody Jet" for domestic flights.
Universal Studios Japan.evidence: On February 21, 2001, in preparation for the opening of Universal Studios Japan, All Nippon Airways unveiled the Woody Woodpecker-themed Woody Jet, using the Boeing 767-300, for its domestic flights.

Tokyo Disneyland.text: It and Tokyo DisneySea are the only Disney parks not owned or operated by the Walt Disney Company.
Tokyo Disneyland.evidence: Tokyo Disneyland and its companion park, Tokyo DisneySea, are the only Disney parks in the world not owned or operated by the Walt Disney Company in any capacity.

Shanghai Disneyland.text: Disney owns only 43% of the park; the Shanghai Shendi Group holds the other 57%.
Shanghai Disneyland.evidence: The park covers an area of 3.9 square kilometres (1.5 sq mi), costing 24.5 billion RMB, with Shendi group holding 57% and Disney holding the remaining 43%.

Chimelong Ocean Kingdom.text: It holds the Guinness world record for the largest aquarium in the world.
Chimelong Ocean Kingdom.evidence: The ocean park holds the Guinness world record for being the largest aquarium in the world, it also had the largest aquarium window in the world according to the Guinness World Records, a single acrylic panel measuring 39.6 by 8.3 metres (130 by 27 ft).

Tokyo DisneySea.text: The idea began as "Port Disney", a scrapped Long Beach park with the RMS Queen Mary as its main attraction.
Tokyo DisneySea.evidence: The idea for what eventually became DisneySea was traced to a proposal to build a second theme park in Southern California called "Port Disney" in Long Beach, California, with the RMS Queen Mary as the main attraction. The idea was scrapped after Disney endured financial trouble with the Euro Disney project.

Epcot.text: Walt Disney first imagined EPCOT as a real community of tomorrow, home to 20,000 residents.

Disney's Hollywood Studios.text: Its original landmark was the Earffel Tower, a faux water tower topped with Mickey Mouse ears.
Disney's Hollywood Studios.evidence: The park's original landmark was the Earffel Tower, a faux water tower topped with Mickey Mouse ears.

Disneyland Park.text: To suit the Parisian weather, Michael Eisner ordered 35 fireplaces installed in its hotels and restaurants.
Disneyland Park.evidence: Modifications to the park were made to protect against changes in weather in the Parisian climate. Covered walkways referred to as "arcades" were added, and Michael Eisner ordered the installation of 35 fireplaces in hotels and restaurants.
